correctness.rationale: The p-energy is strictly convex for p>1, so the center is unique. Strict order monotonicity and translation equivariance give the universal bound 2 and strict finite-pair nonattainment when that value is sharp. Solving the two-leaf equation gives the weighted power-mean formula; at p=2 weighted centering gives the exact 2(1-w_min/W) norm and extremizers. For p>2, a zero center residual makes the designated derivative weight zero; for 1<p<2, all-nonzero residual equilibria with some residuals tending to zero make it vanish in the limit. Positive denominators and all parameter ranges were checked; the standalone checker passed exact and numerical witness checks. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: It is a full sharp operator-stability invariant for the canonical weighted p-energy-selected interpolation on an arbitrary-degree natural star family, across every real p>1 and all positive conductances. The two-input bound is not the one-input harmonic smoothing property. A genuine discontinuity of sharp nonlinear stability at the Hilbert exponent, plus strict nonattainment on both sides, is a mathematically meaningful and potentially useful warning in selecting p-Laplacian regularization despite pointwise convergence of the maps.
